name: Diffuse Idiopathic Skeletal Hyperostosis
definition: Non-inflammatory enthesopathic disorder characterized by flowing anterior spinal ligament ossification and extraspinal enthesopathy, often associated with metabolic comorbidity.

typical: Dysphagia may occur in marked cervical disease

redFlags.item: Trauma in ankylosed spine because fractures may be unstable

core: Swallowing symptoms when cervical disease is extensive

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is radiographic in the appropriate clinical context.
investigations.MRI: CT is valuable after trauma because fractures can be subtle and unstable; MRI assesses neural injury.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs show flowing ossification across multiple vertebrae.

green: Maintain mobility and metabolic risk management
amber: Any significant trauma in an ankylosed DISH spine warrants a low threshold for advanced imaging and specialist review.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Asthi/Snayu-stiffness phenotype may be recorded descriptively; DISH is not equivalent to a classical inflammatory disorder.

patientEducation.summary: Non-inflammatory enthesopathic disorder characterized by flowing anterior spinal ligament ossification and extraspinal enthesopathy, often associated with metabolic comorbidity.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
